content:
An elegant self-experiment does not establish a general treatment effect
A personal dietary result can generate a hypothesis while leaving confounding, adherence and generalizability unresolved. The essay admits that a method may fail for a particular reader, which is appropriate. It still needs controlled evidence for the proposed mechanism and the practical prediction; a deeper story alone does not supply it.

quote: without the explicit theory backing it up.
content:
Mechanistic understanding can improve a prediction, if it earns its place
A theory that correctly predicts when a technique works and fails can improve generalization. A story added after the outcome can explain anything and predict little. The useful test is a new, risky prediction checked against data, including unsuccessful cases and competing explanations.

A memory effect cannot be transferred to meal advice without a test
The classic better-ending experiment concerned cold-water discomfort and later preference between episodes. It does not establish that reducing a meal’s size leaves its remembered pleasure unchanged or that dessert is the only relevant variable. The dietary prescription needs a direct test of the actual outcome being promised.
Kahneman et al. (1993)

quote: willpower, mental conflicts, ego depletion, preference reversals,
content:
The confident appeal to ego depletion aged badly
Hagger et al.’s preregistered 23-lab test found d=0.04, 95% CI [−0.07, 0.15], with 2,141 participants. Vohs et al.’s later 36-lab study found a nonsignificant confirmatory d=0.06 with 3,531 participants. These results substantially weaken reliance on a large, dependable depletion effect as an established foundation for advice.
Hagger et al. (2016); Vohs et al. (2021)

quote: a vocabulary of cognitive phenomena that actually exist
content:
The correction is not that fatigue or every depletion effect is imaginary
A separate preregistered 12-lab study by Dang and colleagues found a small effect, d=0.10, with 1,775 participants. The evidence is heterogeneous, and even a reliable sequential-task effect would not uniquely establish a literal resource tank. The warranted update concerns effect size, generality and mechanism; it does not license an equally sweeping denial.
Dang et al. (2021; online 2020)

A small p-value is not a replication certificate
The ASA statement rejects treating significance as a universal quality threshold. For illustration, if only 1% of tested hypotheses are real, power is 80% and the false-positive rate is 1%, only about 45% of significant results would be true positives even before selective reporting. These are stipulated numbers, not an estimate for this literature; they show why the threshold alone cannot do the promised work.
Wasserstein & Lazar / ASA (2016)
